topic: Gradient descent and optimisation for second-year mechanical engineering undergraduates

entry_point.discipline_context: Mechanical engineers often seek the configuration that minimises stored energy while satisfying constraints.
entry_point.rationale: Starting from a familiar mechanical picture makes the optimisation problem concrete before introducing gradients and updates.

chapter_sequence.title: From potential energy to optimisation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce the problem of finding an energy minimum and connect it to stationary points and equilibrium.

chapter_sequence.title: Smoothness, convexity, and the shape of the energy landscape
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain why smoothness and convexity matter for reliable descent.

chapter_sequence.title: Gradient descent as numerical relaxation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Present the update rule and explain step-size selection.

chapter_sequence.title: Convergence behaviour
chapter_sequence.purpose: Compare general and strongly convex convergence rates.

chapter_sequence.title: Momentum, stochastic updates, and second-order ideas
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce practical extensions and the role of curvature.

discipline_bridges.domain_mapping: In a mechanical system, a stable equilibrium is a local minimum of potential energy, while the gradient is the negative of the force.
discipline_bridges.analogy_boundary: The analogy is useful for intuition, but the optimisation formulation is more general because it need not represent a physical force field.

discipline_bridges.domain_mapping: A numerical method that repeatedly nudges the state in the direction of lower energy is analogous to a damped relaxation process.
discipline_bridges.analogy_boundary: The analogy stops being exact once the update uses a chosen learning rate rather than a physical damping law.

implementation_strategy: Use a one-dimensional Python example to connect the mathematical update to executable code.
Keep the code deliberately simple and show the mapping from gradient to update step.
assessment_strategy: Include five exercises that test conceptual understanding, algebraic reasoning, and simple implementation.
Ask learners to identify whether a step is too large, too small, or about right.
